classification.difficultyReason: There are no diagrams or scaffolding, so the student must interpret 'and' as an intersection and combine two inequalities in each part. Parts a and b are routine: keep the stricter bound, or join the bounds into a double inequality, with care over strict versus inclusive endpoints. The hardest essential demands are parts c and d. In c the student must recognise that no value satisfies both conditions. In d they must see that the two inclusive bounds meet at the single value x = 2. These are a short interpretive step beyond reading a given diagram (p5-q5, p6-q8), but they need no new method and no reframing. This is lighter than the multi-step algebraic modelling in A3 and well below the context inequalities p12-q15 and p12-q16.
